newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France signs alliance with Delta, Continental.
newsitem.headline: Air France signs alliance with Delta, Continental.

text.p: French national airline Air France said on Wednesday it had signed letters of intent for a commercial alliance with Delta Airlines and Continental Airlines of the United States.

The long-awaited agreements mark a strategic step in Air France's development and taps the huge U.S. travel market to feed its global network while the U.S. companies will carry the French airline's passengers on their domestic routes.

Air France chairman Christian Blanc announced the signing of the agreements at a board meeting on Wednesday, the company said in a statement. "These agreements crystallise the company's wish to forge a network of global alliances," Air France said.
The alliances allow code-sharing arrangements between Air France and the U.S. companies, which is a low-cost way of gaining more customers without direct investment and using partners' networks.

It means passengers can be issued with a through-ticket by one carrier to be used on its partner airline -- making it possible for airlines to feed passengers to each other without investing in their own routes.

The companies will also harmonise their flight schedules, share a common frequent flyer programme, and provide ground facilities. Delta operates from its hub at Atlanta, Georgia, while Continental works from Houston, Texas and Air France uses Paris Roissy-Charles De Gaulle airport.
